Music driver, called once a frame by the raster interrupt at line $FF (irq_bottom, $33EE). $FF selects the tune: 0 silences the SID ($D418 = 0) and returns. A value other than tune_playing restarts the driver on that tune (music_start_tune). Otherwise it rewrites the filter registers $D418/$D417/$D415/$D416 from their copies and runs the voices (music_voices). Otherwise count down the current note's time (v_note_time); when it runs out the first time, give one more tick and clear the gate unless the note is tied (v_note_flags bit 6); the second time, read the next pattern byte.

Read the pattern byte. $FF ends the pattern: set v_need_pattern, step v_seq_pos past the "01 nn" pair and read the next sequence command. $80-$FE selects instrument (byte AND $7F) through music_instrument and reads on. $00-$7F is a note: low nibble the note (0 a rest, 1-12 an entry of note_freq_table, which holds the low byte with a high byte of 1), bits 4-6 the octave (added to v_octave_add; the frequency is doubled once per octave). The byte after a note is its length: low nibble an entry of note_length_table (entry $0E also skips the release tick), bits 6-7 the note's flags (v_note_flags). One byte per move 0-$18: what happens when the stick asks for another move while this one runs ($2CDC), when its script ends ($2D3E) and when a hit lands on the fighter making it ($300C). 0 (the attacks other than the flying kick, the duck 4, the blocks $13 and $14, and moves $12 and $15): the move holds its last pose while the stick stays put, plays backwards to the stance when it changes, and is stopped by a hit. 1 (moves 0 and 1, the stance, the jump 5, moves 8 and 9, the flying kick $0E, and $16 and $17): the move runs to its end and the fighter returns to the stance, and a hit does not stop it. $80 (the two walks, 2 and 3): the move changes at once, and a hit puts the fighter in the stance for a step.

One byte per move 0-$18: 1 for the eleven attacking moves (6, 7, $0A-$11, $18), 0 for the rest. Read by the computer's choice ($2559), the collision check ($2A86) and the move code ($2D93, $2DC5, $2DE8).

One byte per move 0-$18: for an attack, the move that defends against it: $13 or $14 (the two blocks), or $05 (a jump) against the sweeps $0A and $10; 0 for the moves that do not attack. A player pulling back as an attack comes within reach is given the block ($2DA3), except against the two sweeps; the computer reads it at $2568 and $2614 and jumps the sweeps too.

One byte per move: 1 for moves 3, 9, $0F and $10, 0 for the rest. For an attack ($0F and $10) it means the move strikes behind the fighter, so the hit test ($2E6B, $2EEF) and the block check ($2FCC, $2FFA) measure the distance the other way, and the fall it causes is $1A ($2F4D, $2FA2). The table is 21 bytes: moves $15-$18 read the first four bytes of full_hit_margin, all 0.

One byte per move 0-$18: how much closer than the strike's reach the other fighter may stand for the strike still to score a full point (the hit test, $2E79 and three other readers). A strike exactly at its reach always scores a full point; farther away it misses.
One byte per move 0-$18: the wider margin within which a strike that is too close for a full point still scores a half point (read at $2E82 and three other places); closer still, it misses.
$11F9-$120D: 21 bytes nothing reads, laid out like a move table: 1 for moves 7, $0A, $0B, $0C and $11, 0 for the rest.

Two bytes per move 0-$18: the address of the move's first strike table (59 bytes, one per pose: $80 = this pose does not strike, otherwise the reach); 0 for moves that never strike. Read at $2E20 into ($8C).

Builds fighter X's head sprite: toggles its buffer ($2D,X), sets its pointer $1A,X to $25 + buffer, then copies the 63-byte head image (at $C000 when $2F,X has bit 7 set, else image $2F,X of the fighter's head set at $33/$35,X). When the image's mirror flag ($37,X) differs from the facing the copy is mirrored through mirror_table; when $39,X is set it is turned upside down too.
Turns the sprite at ($3D) upside down: swaps each of its first 30 bytes with the byte in the mirrored row (vflip_row_partner).

For fighter X's pose $6F,X: the head image (head_flags low nibble minus 1, or a negative number for none) into $2F,X, its X offset (head_x) into $1C,X and its Y offset (head_y) into $1E,X, and from head_flags bit 7 into $20,X, bit 4 the mirror flag into $37,X and bit 5 the upside-down flag into $39,X.
30 bytes: for each byte offset 0-29 of a sprite, the offset of the byte in the mirrored row (row r with row 20 - r, three bytes a row). Read by flip_sprite_shape_vertically.
Per fighter: the first byte of the current script step; bit 7 set makes the position move on every step of its wait, not only on the first.

Unpacks the picture of location $CB AND 3 into the picture band, which ends at $F53F (bitmap rows 5-16). The data's first two bytes give its length; unpacking starts from the end and works backwards: a byte n below $80 copies the n bytes before it, a byte $80 + n repeats the byte before it n times, and 0 ends.
Add the length to the start: (src) now points at the data's last byte.
The destination works down from $F53F.
Next control byte, read backwards.
A run: repeat the byte before the control byte n AND $7F times.
Moves the destination ($54) back by the count in $56.
Moves the source ($52) back by the count in $56 plus one (the carry is clear).
The four pictures' packed data: $3CE2 (location 0), $46F4, $5572 and $6092 (location 3).
picture_ptrs read one byte on, for the high bytes.
The four pictures' packed colours: $6D4A, $6F25, $7101 and $72E9.
colour_ptrs read one byte on, for the high bytes.

Unpacks the colours of location $CB AND 3 for the picture band (rows 5-16) in three passes over one stream of four-bit values: the colour RAM from $D8C8, then the high and the low halves of the screen's colour bytes from $CCC8.
Pass 1: nibbles into colour RAM, low half.
Pass 2: into the screen's high halves.
Pass 3: into the screen's low halves.
One pass: a nibble n gives a count n AND 7 (0 ends the pass); with bit 3 clear the next count nibbles are copied one by one, with bit 3 set the next nibble is written count times.
Bit 3 clear: copy count nibbles.
Bit 3 set: one nibble, count times.
Reads the next nibble into $5F and A, low half first, then the high half, then the next byte; the mask $60 alternates between $0F and $F0.
Writes nibble $5F into the half of ($54) that the mask $61 leaves free, keeping the other half, and moves on a byte.

Start-up: interrupts off, samples on ($EE), no tune ($FF), the keyboard off ($E2), the interrupt vectors (setup_vectors), the sample period tables copied from $C700/$C800 to $0200/$0300, the video chip (setup_vic), the random seed $53, and location 1 marked as the one in the picture band ($D2).
Colour RAM of the status rows 0-4 ($D800-$D8C7) set to white.
Status rows 0-4 of the screen ($CC00-$CCC7) set to spaces.

Fills both colour sources of rows 17-24 with the floor colour (the operand at $1B75, set per location by load_location): colour RAM $DAA8-$DBFF and screen $CEA8-$CFFF. The fill runs on to $CFFF, over the sprite pointers, which the raster interrupt writes again each frame.
The operand: the floor colour, written by load_location ($21F5).

Interrupt set-up: CIA 1 interrupts off, the raster interrupt on, $01 = $05 (I/O in, RAM under the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs), IRQ vector $34CF, reset vector $1BD5 (an RTI), CIA 2's timer B as the only NMI source, NMI vector $32C4, timer B's latch $16BC (5,820 cycles; the raster interrupt at $32A7 starts it), and port A of CIA 1 as inputs.
The reset vector's target: RTI.

Video set-up: bank 3 ($DD00 = 0), screen $CC00 and bitmap $E000 ($D018 = $38), a blank sprite at $C000, a multicolour bitmap ($D011 = $3B, $D016 = $18), raster compare $FF, sprite multicolours 0 and $0A, every sprite multicolour, on and in front, the floor and status colours, the status rows cleared, and the colour RAM of the point symbols' cells (rows 0 and 1, columns 3, 4, 6, 7 and 32, 33, 35, 36) light blue.
The fighters' body colours $41/$42, for the sprites below the heads (2 and 9, red and brown), until init_fighter_side sets them.

Puts both fighters at their starting places for a bout: fighter 0 at X $3E facing right, fighter 1 at X $5A facing left, both at height $50 making move $17 (the opening bow); clears the move state, the hold and step flags and the sprite buffer toggles; 8 steps a struck fighter holds still before its fall ($A2/$A3); then for each fighter init_fighter_side and the computer's level (ai_set_level), and shows the energies.
Fighter X at the start of a bout: energy 127, and from its type $31,X (0-4): the head sprite colour ($2B,X), the body colour ($41,X) and the head set's address ($33,X/$35,X).
Head sprite colour by type 0-4: white, red, dark grey, green, white.
Low bytes of the head sets by type: $B8C0, $B700, $BA80, $BC40 and $BE00 (with type_heads_hi), each seven 64-byte images.
High bytes of the head sets.
Body colour by type 0-4: red, brown, dark grey, red, brown.
Fighter X: no reaction ($7B), no hold ($90), and move $17, the opening bow.

Plays a bout until it ends: both fighters reset, then one step at a time (step_flag is cleared by the raster interrupt, so at most one step a frame): each fighter's input and move (fighter 1 first), the random number, the function keys, the clock while nobody is falling and fighter 0 has finished the opening bow, and the energies. Returns with the keys' $80 (start pressed during the demo), the fall that ended the bout ($7A), or, when the clock runs out, 1 with both fighters standing in pose $37.
Waits while paused (RESTORE) or until the raster interrupt has cleared step_flag.
Fighter 1's turn ($85 = 0, the other fighter), then fighter 0's.
The clock runs only while neither fighter is reacting to a hit and fighter 0's move is no longer the opening bow $17.
Time up: both fighters stand in pose $37.
The entry's target: init_training, then the title loop.
An RTS nothing reaches.
Clears the sprite at $C000 (63 bytes), shown as the empty head.
The random number $B5: shifted left, and EORed with $1D when a 1 falls out.

A two-player game: both fighters human, fighter 0 type 0 and fighter 1 type 1, scores cleared, tune 3. Four rounds, one in each location ($CB 0-3), each lasting the whole 60 seconds; then the higher score wins and bows, a draw makes both bow, and the winner's score is checked against the two-player high score.
One round: the clock at 60, the location's picture, then two_player_bout.
After four rounds: compare the scores.
Bouts until the clock runs out: each time one fighter falls, the other scores the points of the last hit again (add_score), and the fighters start again at full energy.

A one-player game against the computer: the player is fighter 0 (type 0), the computer fighter 1 (type 1-4 in turn), scores cleared, the computer's score hidden, rank NOVICE, tune 2. Each opponent must be beaten twice ($D1); then the rank goes up a dan, the computer's level ($D0) rises by one and the location changes. Once the rank is 10TH DAN, the game goes on for ever (one_player_endless). A loss ends the game and the high score is checked.
One bout: points and tallies cleared, the clock at 60, the location's picture, then one_player_bout.
The player won: one more win needed, or the next opponent.
A draw ($81): both bow and the bout is fought again.
The player lost: high score, then back to the title.
Past the 10th dan: $CB becomes $20 + the next location, and each opponent gets a random level from 7 to 10; the rank stays at 10TH DAN.

One bout of a one-player game: a fall ends it, and the winner bows; when the player wins, the time left is added as a bonus (time_bonus). When the clock runs out the fighter with more energy wins. Returns 1 when the player won, 0 when the computer won, $81 on equal energy.

The demonstration: two computer fighters of random types (0-3 and 1-4) and random levels from 3 to 11 (the AND #7 and ADC #3 add the carry next_ai_random leaves), DEMO at the bottom left, tune 1, one bout in each of the four locations, until F1 or fire.
Stores $FF at $04F0, the end mark of the demo tune's pattern 4, which already holds $FF.
One demonstration bout: a fall ends it and the winner bows; returns $80 when F1 or fire was pressed.

$1FEF-$2097: nothing calls this. It adds the hit's points (1 for a half point, 2 for a full one) to fighter X's tally $A6,X and draws the tally as round point symbols, whole (characters $21-$24) or half ($25-$28), in rows 0 and 1, then compares it with 4: the scoring of The Way of the Exploding Fist, two full points to win a bout. Training keeps clearing the symbols' cells (clear_points) and the tallies $A6/$A7, but never draws them.
Draws a whole point symbol at row 0, column 3 + Y.
Draws a half point symbol at row 0, column 3 + Y.
Clears the point symbols' cells: rows 0 and 1, columns 3, 4, 6 and 7 from Y (0 for fighter 0, $1D for fighter 1).
Fighter X starts move $19, the bow of a winner, at height $50, played forwards.
Fighter X bows: its move is stepped once a frame until it ends.
Both fighters bow, after a draw.

Reads keyboard row 0 once per change: F1 or the fire button of joystick port 2 starts a game ($80) and F3 switches between one and two players, F7 between the joystick and the keyboard and DEL turns the samples on and off, all only at the title (in play, $CC); F5 at any time goes back to the title, with a JMP that leaves the calls it came through on the stack.
No key: fire on port 2 starts a game when not in play.
F3: one or two players.
F7: joystick or keyboard.
F5: back to the title.
DEL: samples on or off.
The title: mode, control and high score shown, the scores cleared, then the demonstration until a game is started; then the game the mode chooses, and back here.
Clears the picture band $E640-$F53F, writing through the operand at $21B8, which the code holds as $1234 and sets to $E640 first.
The operand's low byte, set to $40.
The operand's high byte: $E6 at the start, raised by one for each page.

When location $CB AND 3 is not the one shown ($D2): the band's and the floor's backgrounds are first set to the status background $C9, so the screen below the status rows is one colour while the band is cleared and the location's colours and picture unpacked; then the location's colours: the band's background ($32BE), the status background $C9, the border, and the floor colour ($1B75, $32CB) filled into rows 17-24.
The picture band's background colour by location: light grey, green, blue, blue.
Border colour by location: blue, brown, red, black.
Floor colour by location, the same colour in both halves of a colour byte: yellow ($77), blue, brown, blue.

The status rows' background colour by location ($C9): light blue, light blue, blue, black. irq_bottom sets it ($33E5), and load_location gives the band and the floor the same colour while the next picture is unpacked.
Sets a score to "     0": row 1 from column X (9 for fighter 0, $19 for fighter 1).
Compares the two scores digit by digit (a space counts below a digit). X = 0 when fighter 0's is higher, 1 when fighter 1's is, $80 when they are equal.
In a one-player game fighter 0's score, in a two-player game fighter X's, replaces the mode's high score when it is higher.
Carry clear when the score at row 1, column X is higher than the high score at ($DB).
Copies the score at row 1, column X over the high score at ($DB).

Adds the points of move $A8, the last that landed, to the score at row 1, column X: move_points hundreds, halved unless the hit was a full point ($8A for fighter 0, $8B for fighter 1, 2 for a full point). The tens digit becomes 0 the first time.
Adds 100 to the score at row 1, column X: the hundreds digit goes up, carrying into the thousands and on; a space becomes 1. Past 999,900 all six digits become 0.
The mode's high score at row 4, column 17.
The clock: every 50 steps the two-digit time at row 1, columns 19-20, goes down by one (60, 59 ... 10, then " 9"); after 60 such seconds $D8 is set, time up.
$23A4-$23B5: nothing calls this. It adds move $A8's points, halved for a half point, to fighter X's tally $D9,X; Training clears $D9/$DA before each bout and never reads them.
The clock's digits to "60".
"1 PLAYER" or "2 PLAYER" at row 4, column 31.
Spaces over the rank (row 4, columns 0-7) and the control (row 3, columns 31-38).
"DEMO" at row 4, column 0.
Waits X times six frames (the raster reaching line $FE).
After the player wins before the clock runs out: the clock runs on a second at a time, adding 100 to the player's score for each second left, with a pause between.
Writes rank X at ($DB) + $E6 ($E6 is always 0): NOVICE for 0, 10TH DAN for 10, otherwise the digit with ST, ND, RD or TH and " DAN".
Spaces over the rank at row 4, columns 0-7.
"JOYSTICK" or "KEYBOARD" ($E2) at row 3, column 31.
"JOYSTICK".
"KEYBOARD".
"NOVICE " (seven characters, the space clearing the eighth cell).
"10TH DAN".
The rank shown for each computer level $D0 0-11: NOVICE (0), then the same number up to 10, and 10 again for 11.
Takes A from the energy of the other fighter ($85), stopping at 0; A is written into the SBC's operand at $2514.
The SBC's operand: the energy to take, written at $250C.
Fighter 0's energy at row 0, column 0, fighter 1's at column 37.

The computer's choice for fighter X, into $7F,X and $AC,X (the move it keeps asking for). While the other fighter falls: back to the stance, at once from a flying kick, otherwise after $BD,X steps. While a plan runs ($B9,X): its next step (ai_run_plan). While the other fighter attacks: keep a block that fits it or answer the attack; otherwise ai_idle.
The other fighter's move is an attack: a block that fits it is kept, one that does not is dropped for the stance.
Not blocking: from the stance or a walk, answer the attack (ai_answer); a held or returning move is let go; against a sweep ($0A, $10) the computer stands up unless it is already low.
Keep asking for ai_kept_move,X.

The other fighter attacks: nothing unless the attack can reach (in_range). Then a delay of random AND $C8 steps ($C6,X counts; none at levels 4 and up), then random AND $B8 decides: bit 7 an attack of its own (ai_attack), bits 4-6 the block that fits (ai_block), all clear move $0B or 9 at random, otherwise the plan ai_counter_plan gives for that attack, or the block when it gives none.
Asks for the block that fits the other fighter's attack (move_block).

No attack to answer: a returning move goes on; a held duck is kept; a turn ($12) completes and the facing flips; any other held pose is let go after 5 + random AND $A9 steps ($AA,X counts); from the stance or a walk, the distance decides (ai_approach); otherwise keep the move.

The distance to the other fighter, measured the way fighter X faces. Facing each other: from $D5 to $14 (close, either side) ready to attack (ai_ready), other values from $80 the other fighter is behind (turn round), the rest too far (walk). Facing the same way: from $DF to $1E ready, other values from $80 walk, the rest turn round.

Too far: walk forwards (2) for random AND $C4,X steps (256 when that comes out 0, since the count is decremented before it is tested), then stand for random AND $C2,X steps (or walk on at once when that is 0), and again ($C0,X counts).
Turn round: move $12, with $B6,X set so that ai_idle flips the facing when the turn is held.
Close enough: stand for random AND $B3 steps ($B1,X counts), then attack.

Chooses an attack. Against the block $13 one of 6, $0D, $0E or $11 at random, against $14 one of 7, $0B, $0C or $18 (7 as plan 5, through a duck); otherwise from ai_dist_face (facing each other) or ai_dist_back (facing the same way) by distance, offset by random AND $B0, and swapped for a low attack when the other fighter is low (ai_low_check).
$277D-$277F: a JMP $2674 that nothing reaches.
A flying kick from the table: levels 7 and up walk forwards instead.
A sweep ($0A): levels 0 and 1 make no new choice.
Move 7: duck first, through plan 5.
A back attack ($0F or $10) is made only sometimes: random AND $BF with bit 7 set turns round instead, from $40 walks back (3), from $20 makes move 8.
The computer's random number $B4: shifted left, and EORed with $1D when a 1 falls out. Seeded from $B5 at the start of each game.

Sets the computer's parameters from fighter X's level $CF,X (0-11): the masks $A9, $B0, $B3, $B8, $BF and $C8 and the fall wait $BD/$BE, and for fighter X alone the walk masks $C4,X and $C2,X and the delay $C6,X; the counters start again. Only those three stores are indexed by X, so the second call (fighter 1's, in reset_bout) leaves both fighters with fighter 1's masks: in the demo, both computer fighters play with fighter 1's level except for walking and the code that tests the level itself.
Plan 1: duck (4) until the other fighter stands (move 1), or, at levels 7 and up, until it shows pose $19; then sweep ($0A) and end.
Plan 3: the flying kick $0E, and end.
Plan 4: move 9, and end.
Plan 5: duck (4); once the duck is held, move 7, and end.

Plan 8: plan 5 or plan 6 at random, each step. Choosing plan 5 stores 5 in $B9 without X, which is fighter 0's plan: the computer as fighter 1 stays on plan 8, and in the demo fighter 0 is handed plan 5.
Plan 6: move 6 or $18 at random, and end.
Plan 7: move $10 when the fighters face each other, $0A otherwise, and end.
Plan 2: sweep ($0A), ending once the sweep runs.
Jumps to plan $B9,X through ai_plans.
When the other fighter is low (move 4, 7, $0A or $10), move A becomes ai_low_swap's entry for it.
Plan 9: at levels 7 and up, half the time move $0D and end; otherwise plan 1.

80 moves the computer picks from when the fighters face each other, read as $2934 + distance + $33 + random AND $B0 (distance $D5-$14, so entries 8-$4E). From the other fighter well behind to ahead: the back attacks $0F and $10, then walks, then moves 6, 7, $11 and $18, then $0A-$0E, then the stance.
79 moves for the fighters facing the same way, read as $2984 + distance + $29 + random AND $B0 (distance $DF-$1E).
Addresses of plans 1-9 (plan 0, 0, is never jumped through).
ai_plans read one byte on, for the high bytes.

The plan that answers each attack, by the other fighter's move: 6 → 8, 7 → 2, $0A → 4, $0B → 3, $0C → 2, $0E → 9, $0F → 4, $10 → 7, $11 → 2, $18 → 6; 0 (block instead) for $0D and the moves that do not attack.
The four attacks tried against the block $13: 6, $0D, $0E, $11.
The four attacks tried against the block $14: 7, $0B, $0C, $18.
By level 0-11: $A9, the mask for how long a held pose is kept, and the fall wait $BD/$BE ($1F at levels 0-1, $0F at 2-5, 7 from 6).
By level: $B0, the random spread added to the distance when choosing an attack (7 at levels 0-4, 3 from 5).
By level: $B3, the mask for the wait before an attack when close.
By level: $C4,X, the mask for how long a walk lasts; 11 bytes, so level 11 reads lvl_pause_mask's first.
By level: $C2,X, the mask for the pause between walks.
By level: $BF, the mask that decides whether a back attack is made (ai_back_attack).
By level: $B8, the mask that decides how an attack in reach is answered (ai_answer): level 4's $70 answers only with a block (or move $0B or 9), level 7's $0F never with an attack of its own.
By level: $C8, the mask for the delay before answering ($1F, $0F, 7, 3, then 0 from level 4).

One step for fighter X ($85 is the other): the strike check, the input, the automatic block, the move's state, its script and its end. Then, while sprites 0-2 touch nothing ($D01E), the fighter making an attack is drawn in front ($24), or the other one during move $11.
The move fighter X asks for, into $7F,X: its current move while hold_steps runs, its reaction ($7B,X) after a hit, else the computer's choice (ai_move), the keyboard (F7) or the joystick.

Fighter 0 reads joystick port 2 ($DC00), fighter 1 port 1 ($DC01). The five bits index joy_moves; for a fighter facing left, left and right are swapped first (unless both are held), so that the table's right is always forwards.

The move for each reading of the stick (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire, 0 when pressed), facing right. Without fire: up 5, down 4, forwards 2, back 3, up and forwards 6, down and forwards 7, down and back 8, up and back 9. With fire: up $0E, down $0A, forwards $0C, back $11, up and forwards $0D, down and forwards $0B, down and back $10, up and back $0F. Nothing, or fire alone: the stance 1.

The keyboard (F7): the same reading built from keys, then joy_moves. Fighter 0 uses Q W E, A D, Z X C for the eight directions and S or the left SHIFT for fire; fighter 1 uses P @ *, L ;, , . / and : or the right SHIFT.
Fighter 0's fire: S or the left SHIFT clears bit 4 ($E1).
Fighter 0's direction, as the low four bits of a stick reading: Q, E, Z, W, C, X, D, A in that order of testing.
Fighter 1's fire: the right SHIFT or :.
Fighter 1's direction: /, *, P, @, ,, ., L, ; in that order of testing.

Decides fighter X's current move $7D,X from the one asked for ($7F,X). A fall ($16, $1A or $1B) starts after $A2,X steps held still, at height $50, with sample 3 when a new step shows pose $2C or $28. From the stance a new move starts at once ($11 as $12, and the low attacks 7, $10 and $0A through a duck first); a low attack asked for during a held duck starts at once, during the turn $12 the turn plays backwards, and in any other move it is ignored, so no sweep comes straight out of a walk; the turn $12 and move $11 have their own rules; anything else follows move_let_go.
Another move asked for.
In a move other than the stance.
The turn $12 and move $11.
As move_let_go says: a walk changes at once, a move marked 0 plays backwards to the stance, one marked 1 runs on.

When fighter X's script has ended ($75,X): the other fighter's flying_hit is cleared; a reaction ends the bout ($7A = the fall); a move that played backwards returns to the stance (a low attack to the duck, and move $11 turns the fighter round); one that played forwards holds its last pose or returns to the stance, as move_let_go says.
Back to the duck (4).
$2D5C-$2D62: nothing jumps here: an ADC $14, then 8 into $6B,X and RTS.

Unless hold_steps runs: a fighter pulling back (3) keeps a block it is making, and when the other fighter's attack (other than a sweep $0A or $10, and neither returning nor held) can reach it (in_range), it asks for the block that fits (move_block). Down and forwards (7) asked for out of anything but a duck or move 7 becomes move $18.
7 becomes $18 unless ducking.
Starts the script of fighter X's current move when it changes (sample 2 for an attack), keeps no script while the move is held ($90), then steps the animation (animate_fighter).
When fighter X's attack shows its strike pose (move_strike_pose) on a new step, or on any step for a flying kick that has not yet landed, and the move is neither returning nor held: hit_test.
Takes the move's strike table (strike_table_a when the fighters' facings differ, strike_table_b when they are the same) and tests the hit.
Same facing: the test with the distance measured the other way.

Facings differ: the reach is the strike table's byte for the other fighter's pose ($80: no strike against that pose), the distance from fighter X to the other in its facing direction. Exactly at the reach, or short of it by no more than full_hit_margin, scores a full point; short by no more than half_hit_margin, a half point; past the reach, nothing. A move that strikes behind measures it the other way.
A full point: $8A,X = 2, and move_damage doubled taken from the other fighter.
A half point: $8A,X = 1, and move_damage taken.
Same facing: as ht_facing with the distance's sign turned round.

The hit landed: $A8 = the move; a flying kick marks the other fighter (flying_hit); a human scores (add_score at hit_score_col). If the other fighter's energy is now 0 it falls ($7B,Y). Facings differ: $1A after a move that strikes behind, $1B after moves 7, $0C and $18, $16 after the rest; same facing: $16 after a move that strikes behind, $1A after the rest. Sample 0 goes with $16, sample 1 with $1A and $1B. With energy left: hit_reaction, and the same sample.

A = 1 when the other fighter's attack could reach fighter X. Facings differ: a distance from $EF to $13 (close, either side), unless the attack strikes behind. Same facing: only an attack that strikes behind, from 3 to $1F.

The struck fighter (Y = $85) keeps its energy: standing or walking, it is put in the stance (move 1) and held there for a step (hold_steps); in a move marked 0 by move_let_go, the move is stopped ($90); in one marked 1, nothing.
